fields.title: Cancer of the duodenum
fields.bodyHtml:
Cancer of the duodenum: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the duodenum is a rare condition affecting the first section of the small intestine. Israeli clinics offer innovative approaches to diagnosing and treating this type of cancer, giving patients access to advanced medical technology and the international experience of their specialists.

Diagnosis of cancer of the duodenum

  1. Endoscopy with biopsy (gastroscopy)
    An endoscopic examination allows the inner surface of the duodenum to be seen and tissue samples to be taken for histological analysis
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    These imaging methods are used to assess the stage of the disease and identify metastases.
  3. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count, biochemical tests and tumour marker tests that help in diagnosing the cancer.
  4. PET-CT
    A method that allows the metabolic activity of the tumour to be assessed and metastases in other organs to be identified.

Treatment of cancer of the duodenum

  1. Surgery
    Radical removal of the tumour is the main treatment. Depending on the position and size of the tumour, part of the duodenum and neighbouring organs may need to be removed.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Used to destroy cancer cells, particularly where metastases are present, or to shrink the tumour before surgery.
  3. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, aimed at destroying cancer cells with minimal effect on healthy tissue.
  4. Radiotherapy
    Sometimes used in combination with chemotherapy to control the disease and reduce symptoms.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Israel's leading clinics bring in specialists from various fields to develop a comprehensive treatment plan.
  • Innovative treatments: Patients have access to the latest advances in oncology, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy.
  • Highly qualified specialists: The experience and knowledge of Israeli doctors make treatment highly effective and provide support at every stage.
  • An individual approach: Treatment is planned with the particular features of each case in mind, which makes it possible to achieve the best results.

Choosing Israel for the treatment of cancer of the duodenum gives patients a chance of successful treatment thanks to access to advanced medical technology and the deep professionalism of its doctors.

fields.title: Cancer of the eye socket
fields.bodyHtml:
Cancer of the eye socket (an orbital tumour) is a rare and dangerous condition that requires accurate diagnosis and highly effective treatment. It can affect various structures of the eye socket, including the muscles, nerves and blood vessels, which leads to serious impairment of vision and of the functioning of the eye.

Diagnosis of cancer of the eye socket

  1. Detailed review of the medical history: The doctor talks to the patient about their medical history, including their symptoms, any preceding illness, previous conditions and treatment.
  2. Visual examination: The doctor examines the patient's eyes, noting any changes in the structure of the eye socket and the surrounding tissues.
  3. Ophthalmoscopy: Using special instruments, the doctor assesses the state of the optic nerve, the vessels of the fundus and the retina.
  4. Computed tomography (CT): Produces detailed images of the structure of the eye socket, reveals the presence of a tumour and allows its size and position to be assessed.
  5. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): Used for a more precise assessment of the structure of the tumour and its relationship to the surrounding tissues.
  6. Biopsy: Taking a sample of tumour tissue for histological examination, which helps establish the type of tumour and how malignant it is.
  7. Ultrasound examination of the eye: Allows assessment of the structure of the eyeball and the optic nerve and identification of possible changes in the eye socket.
  8. Doppler ultrasound of the vessels of the eye: Used to assess the blood supply in the vessels of the eye and identify possible abnormalities associated with cancer of the eye socket.

Treatment of cancer of the eye socket

Cancer of the eye socket is treated in Israel using the most modern and innovative methods. The main treatments include:

  1. Surgery: The main treatment, aimed at removing the tumour. Depending on the size and position of the tumour, various types of operation are possible, including minimally invasive techniques.
  2. Radiotherapy: Used to destroy cancer cells, to shrink the tumour before an operation, or to prevent recurrence after surgery. Modern equipment is used to deliver precise and safe radiotherapy.
  3. Chemotherapy: The use of medicines to destroy cancer cells. It may be used on its own or in combination with surgery and radiotherapy.
  4. Immunotherapy: A modern treatment aimed at activating the patient's immune system to fight the cancer cells, using medicines that strengthen the immune response to the tumour.
  5. Targeted therapy: The use of medicines that act on specific molecules involved in the growth and development of cancer cells. This method minimises damage to healthy tissue.

Advantages of treating cancer of the eye socket in Israel

  1. A high level of medical expertise: Israel is home to leading specialists in oncology and ophthalmology with many years of experience and unique skills.
  2. Modern equipment: Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach: Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments: The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including immunotherapy and targeted therapy.
  5. Comfortable conditions: Patients can expect a high standard of comfort and service during treatment and rehabilitation.

Treatment of cancer of the eye socket in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves the outlook.

fields.title: Breast cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Breast cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers in women worldwide. Israel has developed and successfully applies advanced approaches to diagnosing and treating this disease, combining innovative medical technology with highly qualified specialists, including the use of tumour marking for precise guidance during treatment.

Diagnosis of breast cancer

  1. Mammography
    The main method of early detection of breast cancer, allowing tumours to be identified at an early stage.
  2. Ultrasound scan
    Used for further examination of areas of the breast that have raised suspicion on mammography.
  3. Breast MRI
    A highly informative method, particularly recommended for women at high risk of developing breast cancer.
  4. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample for histological analysis is the definitive way of confirming the diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  5. PET-CT
    A method combining PET and CT to assess accurately how far the cancer has spread, determine the stage of the disease and judge the effectiveness of treatment.
  6. MRI-guided tumour marking
    This method allows the position of the tumour in the breast to be established precisely, which makes planning treatment and surgery easier.

Treatment of breast cancer

  1. Surgery
    Includes lumpectomy (removal of the tumour while preserving the breast) and mastectomy (removal of the whole breast). The choice depends on the stage of the disease and the patient's wishes.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Given after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used both before and after surgery to reduce the risk of recurrence and destroy cancer cells in the body.
  4. Hormone therapy
    Prescribed for patients with hormone-dependent breast cancer, to block the effect of oestrogen on the cancer cells.
  5. Targeted therapy
    Involves the use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  6. Immunotherapy
    The newest treatment, stimulating the body's immune system to fight the cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel

Israel attracts patients from all over the world for a number of reasons:

  • Multidisciplinary teams of specialists, including oncologists, surgeons, radiologists and geneticists.
  • An individual approach to the treatment of every patient, taking account of every aspect of her health.
  • Access to innovative treatments and the latest clinical research.
  • A high standard of medical care and attention to patients' comfort.

Innovative approaches and highly qualified specialists make Israel one of the world leaders in the treatment of breast cancer, offering patients not only treatment but hope of a full recovery.

fields.title: Lip cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Lip cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Lip cancer is a malignant growth affecting the outer layers of the skin or the mucous membrane of the lips. In Israel, patients are offered an advanced and comprehensive approach to treating this disease, delivering high effectiveness and a minimal risk of recurrence.

Diagnosis of lip cancer

  1. Visual examination and palpation
    The first diagnostic method, allowing abnormalities on the lips to be detected.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample from the suspicious area for histological examination.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests and tumour markers
    Blood tests are carried out to establish general indicators of health and specific biomarkers associated with cancer.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    These help assess how deeply the tumour has penetrated and whether there are metastases.
  5. Ultrasound scan
    Used to assess the state of the regional lymph nodes of the neck and the surrounding tissues.
  6. PET-CT for a comprehensive assessment
    This method makes it possible to assess not only the position and size of the tumour but also the metabolic activity of the tissue, which is critically important for staging the cancer and planning treatment.

Treatment of lip cancer

  1. Surgery
    The main treatment, aimed at removing the tumour together with enough surrounding healthy tissue to minimise the risk of recurrence.
  2. Radiotherapy
    May be given either before or after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used less often, mainly to treat advanced forms of lip cancer or metastases.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest approaches to treatment, directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells and at activating the immune system to fight the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Doctors in Israel have international experience and constantly develop their skills through scientific research.
  • An individual approach
    Every patient is given a personalised treatment programme that takes account of every feature of their condition and their preferences.
  • Advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment
    The use of the most modern technology and treatments makes the therapy as effective as possible.
  • Multidisciplinary teams
    Specialists of various kinds take part in treatment, which ensures a comprehensive approach to fighting the disease.

Israeli clinics offer patients with lip cancer access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified care, which makes it possible to achieve the best treatment results and considerably improve quality of life after therapy.
